event: A creak and thud sound occurs as the front door is closed.

sounding_object.description: A dark brown, solid wood, arched-top front door. It features a small, narrow, vertical rectangular glass pane in its upper section. A black, lever-style door handle is on its right side (when viewed from the interior). A white, rectangular security sensor component is visible on the top right of the door frame, with its corresponding part on the door itself. The door opens inwards. Approximate size: standard exterior door height (~2 meters or 6.6 feet), width (~0.8-0.9 meters or 2.6-3 feet).

reference_object.description: The first-person perspective of the camera wearer. This is the origin point for egocentric calculations.

facing_object.description: A man with curly brown hair, wearing glasses, a light blue short-sleeved collared shirt, and dark shorts. He is holding a phone and has earphones around his neck. At the moment of the sound, the camera is primarily facing him as he walks into the room.

question: Imagine you are the camera wearer, when the creak and thud sound comes up, relative to where you are facing, where is the sound source: front-left, front-right, back-left, or back-right? The directions refer to the quadrants of a Cartesian plane (if you are standing at the origin and facing along the positive y-axis). Consider the center point location of the object as the its location.
